newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Elusive Romanian MPs to get mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Elusive Romanian MPs to get mobile phones.

text.p: Romanian members of parliament are to be given mobile phones at taxpayers' expense to enable staff to track them down and cut absenteeism in sessions, a Bucharest daily said on Thursday.

The paper, Adevarul, said the Chamber of Deputies would buy 350 phones to keep in contact with members in their constituencies or when moving around the vast "Palace of Parliament", built in the 1980s by Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
It estimated the cost to the public purse at the equivalent of $175,000. But the daily said the innovation was unlikely to increase attendance as members could simply ignore unwanted calls.

Members have been criticised for failing to show up in sufficient numbers to pass reform legislation in the palace -- the world's second largest building after the Pentagon in Washington, with 3,600 telephones.
Some members make a token appearance and turn over their identity cards to colleagues who cast several ballots at once.
Only 20 percent of the country's 23 million people have access to a telephone and residents often wait years to get connected to the network.
